Beginning to analyze how frontend API requests are authenticated.

wc/connect.ts likely contains the auth interceptor and token refresh logic. web/src/auth-state.ts probably handles token storage. server/auth/ likely contains the backend validation package. Reading these files now to confirm exact paths and token types.

Checking auth-state.ts to identify token types and the server/auth package structure.

The frontend interceptor is web/src/connect.ts. It sends a Bearer access token in the Authorization header and stores a refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie via credentials: include. Backend validation lives in the server/auth package. Authenticator is wired through Authorizer and the Connect AuthInterceptor and gateway middleware in v1.go.

Found the auth interceptor at `web/src/connect.ts` (`authInterceptor`). It manages an access token stored in localStorage and a refresh token kept as an HttpOnly cookie. The backend package `server/auth` validates these tokens.
Checking auth_service_session to locate the refresh cookie.
Searching for the Authorizer file to locate the auth interceptor.
Checking acl_config and other files for the Authorizer.

The backend package that validates tokens is `server/auth`, containing an `Authenticator`.

The frontend interceptor lives at `web/src/connect.ts`. It manages a short-lived JWT access token stored in localStorage and an HttpOnly refresh token sent via `credentials: include`. A backend `Authorizer` in `authz.go` wraps the `server/auth` package for Connect/gRPC.
